objective:
Make Agentopia's Windows desktop interface and agent behavior match ChatGPT/Codex Desktop as closely as practical. Use the actual Codex harness for ChatGPT OAuth and compatible OpenRouter connections, retaining OpenRouter support and using it sparingly for paid tests. Prefer connected ChatGPT OAuth models by default, with a user setting when both providers are connected. 



Preserve PostgreSQL/Supabase, existing accounts, passwords, history, and data through recoverable upgrades. Complete and verify the chat-first interface, multiple sidebars, right-side file/folder navigation and document/canvas/browser workspace, model and thinking controls, permissions, implicit consent for explicitly attached context, inline goals with edit/delete/pause/resume/expand and no default turn limit, default queued messages with explicit steering, parallel chats, skills/plugins with validated schemas, and independent background subagents with child chats, live collapsible activity, steering, cancellation, results, and reports back to the main agent. 



Provide working browser and computer-use capabilities plus command-line/script execution through the chat interface. Coordinate authorized parallel Agentopia chats to avoid conflicting edits, builds, and restarts. Validate actual installed behavior and recovery; distinguish completed implementation from demonstrated capabilities and remaining parity work. Immediate step: finish the user-approved verified 0.44.17 Windows update, reopen the ordinary profile, verify preserved data and connections and the goal/queue controls, then continue the remaining desktop parity work.



Ensure you are screenshotting ChatGPT Desktop, testing its features and comparing against Agentopia so you know the functions and features work the same, and the design is the same. Obviously we also have the goal of adding in the workspace agent functionality from the other chat, so we will work on that after our agentopia platform is on par.



Can the agent work on its own?

Do permissions work properly? Can agents work autonomously?

Do subagents work the same?

Are we using the correct harnesses for Codex, OpenRouter, etc?

Can chats read other chats similar to how codex can coordinate between chats?

- Can it create images? Can it read images?
- Can it create documents? Can it read documents?
- Can it create PDFs? Can it read PDFs?
- How about spreadsheets, etc?

- Do they maintain identity?
- Do they have skills, sops, tools, etc they can use?
